question.text: An 'Accredited Investor' (also called 'Qualified Investor' or 'Professional Investor' globally) is characterised primarily by:

answer.text: Being an individual with a demat account and PAN only
Being an investor of a class that understands financial products, risks/returns, and can take informed decisions — recognised by securities regulators globally
Being an investor with income below Rs 2 lakh per annum
Being a retail investor with a Rs 2 lakh per-application cap

explanation.text: **The Logic:** Per Ch 1.1.4 (iii), Accredited Investors (also Qualified/Professional Investors) are recognised internationally as investors who understand financial products, the associated risks/returns, and can take informed decisions. SEBI has recognised this category in India. **The Trap:** Option A is bare-minimum KYC, not accredited status. Option C describes someone below means-test, not an accredited class. Option D describes a Retail Individual Investor. **Cross-Exam Context:** Cross-links to X-A/X-B (Investment Adviser) where accredited-investor status opens access to SVF Category I AIFs and higher-risk SSE instruments. SIAs cite investor classification when reporting subscriber mix. **Assessor's Pro-Tip:** The accredited-investor framework matters because some SSE instruments (e.g., large-ticket DIBs or SVF units) are restricted to accredited-investor eligibility. Confirm classification when reviewing fund-flow evidence.
